record.title: Parameterized economic-data web skills improve matched transfer, while approximate retrieval erases gains on uncovered tasks
record.summary: In arXiv:2609.19523v1, the authors evaluate 50 reusable procedures for retrieving live economic data from authoritative websites. In a controlled study using gpt-5-mini with BrowserGym, they report that a known matched skill raised success from 41.0% to 49.3% across 100 held-out variants repeated with three seeds. In a separate 360-task library-scale study, retrieving five skills was statistically tied with no-skill prompting overall (28.3% versus 28.1%): it scored 48.0% versus 44.0% on directly covered tasks, but 14.3% versus 16.7% on tasks without a direct match. The preprint therefore reports procedural transfer under a known match while exposing coverage-aware selection as the unresolved deployment problem. These are author-reported results from one benchmark/model/harness configuration, not an independent reproduction or evidence of general web-agent improvement.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_PUBLICATION_EVENT
claims.text: The authors posted arXiv:2609.19523v1 on 2026-09-17 under the title EconSkills: Studying Skill Transfer and Retrieval for Web Agents on Live Economic Data.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the authors’ controlled experiment, one directly matched parameterized skill raised success from 41.0% (123/300) to 49.3% (148/300) across 100 held-out variants and three seeds; the paper reports McNemar p=0.0031.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the separate 360-task library-scale experiment, five retrieved skills scored 28.3% overall versus 28.1% for no-skill prompting, 48.0% versus 44.0% on the 150 directly covered tasks, and 14.3% versus 16.7% on 210 tasks without a direct match.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: Independent reproduction, transfer beyond the tested benchmark and gpt-5-mini/BrowserGym configuration, production reliability, and net economic value are not established by this single preprint.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction or audit of the reported controlled and library-scale episodes was identified in this bounded review.
The studies use one model (gpt-5-mini), one browser-agent ecosystem and EconWebArena economic-portal tasks; generalization to other models, websites and task classes is unknown.
This review did not inspect the released dataset/skill artifacts, raw trajectories or complete execution logs, so artifact consistency and episode-level scoring could not be checked.

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded result is true, it informs design choices for persistent browser agents that repeatedly retrieve economic data: verified parameterized procedures can help when correctly matched, while approximate retrieval can hurt uncovered tasks. Score 4 reflects a meaningful local design implication; evidence is one author-reported benchmark study using one model and harness, with no independent reproduction or demonstrated transfer beyond economic portal tasks.
limitations: Results are reported by the preprint authors and have not been independently reproduced in this review.
The paper reports gpt-5-mini in BrowserGym/AgentLab with a 30-step budget on live EconWebArena economic data tasks; no other model, harness or task domain was tested in the reviewed results.
The controlled transfer study uses three seeds per condition; the library-scale conditions use one run per task and provide no across-seed error bars.
The library contains 50 skills derived from solved seed trajectories across 37 websites and nine of ten benchmark categories; it does not cover all task families.
The overall retrieval condition is statistically tied with baseline, and approximate matches lower success on uncovered tasks; the paper does not establish net production or economic impact.
brief.summary: In arXiv:2609.19523v1, the authors evaluate 50 reusable procedures for retrieving live economic data from authoritative websites. In a controlled study using gpt-5-mini with BrowserGym, they report that a known matched skill raised success from 41.0% to 49.3% across 100 held-out variants repeated with three seeds. In a separate 360-task library-scale study, retrieving five skills was statistically tied with no-skill prompting overall (28.3% versus 28.1%): it scored 48.0% versus 44.0% on directly covered tasks, but 14.3% versus 16.7% on tasks without a direct match. The preprint therefore reports procedural transfer under a known match while exposing coverage-aware selection as the unresolved deployment problem. These are author-reported results from one benchmark/model/harness configuration, not an independent reproduction or evidence of general web-agent improvement.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report a matched-skill success rate of 49.3% versus 41.0% without a skill on 100 held-out variants (three seeds), and report that five-skill retrieval is tied with baseline overall on 360 tasks while doing better on directly covered tasks and worse on tasks without a direct match.
technical.compute_or_cost: Provider tokens, monetary cost and human curation cost were not assessed in this source review.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper itself and its reported experimental tables are publicly available at arXiv:2609.19523v1. No experiment result has been independently demonstrated by this activation.
technical.mechanism: The authors distill successful BrowserGym trajectories into structured, instance-free procedures that encode task scope, preconditions, navigation steps, portal guidance, verification and recovery. The experiments separate known-match transfer from library-scale selection, where the agent receives a full library, five retrieved skills, random skills or an optional hint.
technical.novelty: The useful contribution is the separation of procedural transfer when a correct skill is known from retrieval/coverage effects at library scale, including explicit covered/uncovered results that reveal a failure mode hidden by aggregate scores.
technical.regime: Author-run live EconWebArena tasks across government, banking, markets, labor, finance, energy, education, health and trade portals; gpt-5-mini within BrowserGym/AgentLab, fixed observation/action configuration and 30-step cap. Controlled transfer uses 100 variants with three seeds per condition; library-scale tasks use one run per task.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes reproduction details and links a public EconSkills dataset/artifact. This activation did not inspect artifact contents, pin a release, rerun episodes or locate an independent reproduction.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within the reported study, no-skill prompting is the primary baseline; raw successful-trajectory prompting is included for matched transfer, and random-five, all-50 and optional-hint conditions test library delivery.

brief.title: Parameterized economic-data web skills improve matched transfer, while approximate retrieval erases gains on uncovered tasks
brief.why_it_matters: If reproduced, explicit, parameterized procedures could make recurring agent work on economic portals more reliable and reduce navigation effort. The results also show why retrieval coverage and semantic checks matter: applying a merely approximate procedure to an uncovered task can erase the benefit and lower success. This is a useful, bounded design result for web-agent memory and economics-data workflows, with generalization beyond the tested benchmark still unknown.
